title: What Damla is for
summary: The idea in one page, and a map of the app.
text: damla is a cash-flow app that lives on your iphone. it answers one question every day: will you have enough money until your next income, and what happens if you spend, commit to something or delay something. you tell damla what happens with your money - a sentence, a form, a bank alert or a pasted message. damla keeps the books correctly: every amount moves between two places, so nothing is counted twice. all the maths - balances, instalments, forecasts, gains - is done by ordinary, tested code. the on-device model only helps read your words. your data stays on the phone: there is no account, no server and no tracking. today: the answer first, then what needs you. invented sample data. when to use it every day, to see the one number that matters: how much is safe to spend. before you buy something or commit to a payment, to see what it does to the weeks ahead. when a bank message arrives, so the transaction is recorded without typing it in. when you want to know where the money went, what you own, or whether you can afford something you have in mind. step by step: a look around the app the app has five tabs at the bottom. here is what each one is for. open damla. it asks for face id when you open it, and again only after it has been away for the length of time you choose in settings under basics, ask for face id (every time, or after 1, 5 or 15 minutes). the shortcut automations that pass bank messages to damla do not need it. stay on today . the big teal card shows safe to spend, whether your balance stays above your minimum, and a small chart of your balance ahead (tap it for the full forecast and what if). below it you find what is coming, and anything waiting for you. tap activity to see every transaction. tap one to change it. tap accounts to see your banks, savings, cards, loans, investments, assets and people. tap insights to see where the money went, your budget, net worth and holdings. tap plan to see everything that commits future money: income and bills, instalment plans, staged purchases, bills coming, and people you lent to or owe. on today, the gear icon at the top right opens settings, where you also find the guide, your backup and the set-up guide. the book icon next to it opens the guide directly. good to know note: damla is made so that your books stay right even when you are quick about it. anything that creates a commitment (an instalment plan, a loan) or that damla is unsure about is shown for one tap before it is written. tip: when you have no accounts yet, today shows a let's set up damla screen with a set up step by step button. the set-up guide can be reopened later from today or from settings. note: the app gives you information and estimates about your own spending. it does not give financial advice; what to spend is your decision. if you wonder what reaches the internet at all: no account, balance, transaction or note ever leaves the phone, and the app works fully offline. the only lookups are the few optional ones, and they send no personal data - see privacy and your data . related setting up your books a day with damla forecast and safe to spend the free trial and the title: Type a sentence
summary: Say what happened in your own words and Damla fills the form.
text: type what happened - "lunch 45 at zuma from visa" - and damla reads it into an amount, an account, a category and a date. you check what it found and confirm with one tap; no transaction is saved until you do. it is a form that fills itself in from your own words. if damla reads something wrong or misses a part, you finish the rest in the normal form, starting from what it understood. type a sentence and damla fills the form. when to use it when you just paid for something or received money, and you want to record it without filling a form. when you got a bank message or an email about money that damla did not catch automatically: paste it in. when you want to turn a card purchase into instalments by saying so, for example "school payment on the everyday card, now 6 months". when you want to note a bill: a message that a bill is ready or due, with its amount or a due date, is remembered as a bill coming. step by step tap the plus button on today or activity. tap type a sentence . the add by sentence screen opens with the keyboard ready. write what happened in your own words, with the amount, an account or card name, and a date if it was not today. the example shown in the field is "for example: lunch 45 at zuma from visa". you can also write a commitment, such as putting a purchase on instalments. tap continue . the button shows reading… while damla reads the words, then the section called check and save shows what it found. if everything is right, tap save . if a part is missing or unclear, damla says what it needs and offers complete it , which opens the form with what was understood already filled in; finish it there and save. two shortcuts: paste puts the clipboard in the field and reads it straight away, without another tap. this is for bank texts or emails you copied. a message that arrives from your shortcut, the share sheet or the inbox opens this same screen already read: the first thing you see is the check and save section. what you can see in check and save an ordinary payment or income: the amount, the accounts it moves between, the payee and the date. tap save. something that looks already recorded: the section warns "this looks like something already recorded." and offers save anyway. check it first - paying twice is possible. a purchase turned into instalments: the reading shows the instalment, the number of months, the first date and any fee, with the note "this creates a commitment, so please check it." the button is create plan . it stays a suggestion until you tap it. something incomplete: "i need a bit more:" lists the questions, such as "how much?" or "which account does it come from?", and complete it opens the form. a bill notice: "this is a bill notice." damla remembers it as an expected bill; the card charge that later pays it is the one real transaction, so nothing is counted twice. a card statement notice: "this is a card statement notice." tap review the statement to go through it. if the sentence is actually a bank alert with the amounts printed in the usual shape, code reads it; only sentences that are not shaped like an alert go through the sentence reader. good to know note: where the iphone supports apple intelligence, the on-device model reads your words - nothing is sent anywhere. every amount, name and date the model returns must appear in your sentence or it is ignored, so a number it got wrong cannot creep in silently. the account and category names it returns must match your real accounts, or your own words for them are kept instead. limit: if apple intelligence is not available on your phone, damla uses a simpler on-device reader. the screen says so and asks you to check the result before saving; missing parts open the form with complete it . limit: damla works out better from the names you actually use. if it cannot tell which account you meant, it asks, rather than guessing. note: no transaction or plan is written to your books until you tap save, save anyway or create plan. anything that creates a commitment or that damla is unsure about is always shown for one tap first. after you save, damla remembers how you categorised the payee, so the next message from the same shop is filed in that category on its own. related fill a form paste or share a message the inbox instalment plans

title: Forecast and safe to spend
summary: How Damla works out the amount that is safe to spend, and how to read the chart.
text: the forecast shows your balance for the days ahead, day by day, from what is already in your books. safe to spend is the most you can spend today without your balance falling below your minimum at any point in the coming period. the forecast. when to use it to see how low your balance gets, and when, over the range you pick: 3m, 6m, 1y, 2y or 5y. when today says you may run short, to find the day it happens. after you change an income, a bill or a due date, to see what the weeks look like now. step by step open the forecast from the chart on the teal card at the top of today. pick a range with the picker at the top; the chart draws your balance for it, with your minimum as a dashed red line. touch and drag along the chart to move the dot: a small box shows the day's date, balance and movements, and the card below lists them as money in and money out with totals. read the banner at the top: if and when the balance would fall under your minimum, or that it stays above your minimum. tap what if at the top right to try a change: spend, receive, skip a recurring payment or plan, or add an instalment plan. the effect on safe to spend and the lowest point is shown; nothing is saved to your books. how the number is worked out it counts your income and bills from plan, income & bills, on their schedules; ones you recorded or skipped are not counted again. card bills: statements already issued use their real amount on their due dates; ones not issued yet use a typical month of the card's spending - an average of its recent months, with the number set in settings under expected card spending, or the figure you give in the card's details. an issued statement's real amount takes over, and each card's figure is listed in the cards group under what this forecast is made of. instalment plans, staged payments, bills announced by notices and repayments with people are counted on their dates. everyday spending from your bank accounts is not estimated: that is what your buffer is for. safe to spend looks at least as far ahead as the look ahead setting, counting your next income inside that period too, so a big payment just after payday lowers the number. it is the lowest balance in that period minus the minimum. a worked example an invented household, on 9 november. currency aed, minimum balance aed 1,000, look ahead at least 30 days. what counts value everyday account (bank) aed 29,600 today savings aed 40,000, marked not in forecast internet, monthly on the 12th aed 350 out rent, monthly on the 16th aed 8,000 out salary, monthly on the 27th aed 25,000 in today shows: balance today aed 29,600, lowest point aed 21,250 on mon 16 nov, safe to spend aed 20,250 - the lowest point minus the aed 1,000 minimum. the window looked at runs from 9 nov to 9 dec, past the salary on fri 27 nov, so what lands after payday is counted too. the savings are not in these figures. balance day by day (expected line; cautious is the same here, as every item is fixed): date balance why 9 to 11 nov aed 29,600 12 nov aed 29,250 internet 350 16 nov aed 21,250 rent 8,000 (the lowest point) 27 nov aed 46,250 salary 25,000 one-off payment limits (one payment, keeping the minimum): payment date most you could pay comfortable amount 10 nov, 13 nov or 19 nov aed 20,000 aed 16,000 29 nov (after salary) aed 36,500 aed 29,500 read it like this: before the salary, a payment up to the first row's amounts never takes the balance under the aed 1,000 minimum; after payday leaves a larger limit. good to know note: the chart draws two lines, expected and cautious. cautious delays or discounts income that is not fixed; safe to spend uses that line. outflows are never delayed and an estimated amount is counted at its less favourable end. when nothing in your plan is uncertain, the lines overlap. limit: if a card has no estimate at all, a warning appears above the chart and the forecast is too optimistic: it leaves out what the card will spend after its next statements. give the card a typical month in its details, or import statements. if expected card spending is off in settings, only what is already on your cards is counted. money left out because its account is not in the forecast is named at the top. note: information and estimates, not financial advice. related what if income and bills that repeat ask damla a day with damla
